title: Uses of Electromagnetic Waves

blocks.name: Uses of electromagnetic waves
blocks.definition:
Describe typical uses of the different regions of the electromagnetic spectrum including:
(a) radio waves; radio and television transmissions, astronomy, radio frequency identification (RFID)
(b) microwaves; satellite television, mobile phones (cell phones), microwave ovens
(c) infrared; electric grills, short range communications such as remote controllers for televisions, intruder alarms, thermal imaging, optical fibres
(d) visible light; vision, photography, illumination
(e) ultraviolet; security marking, detecting fake bank notes, sterilising water
(f) X-rays; medical scanning, security scanners
(g) gamma rays; sterilising food and medical equipment, detection of cancer and its treatment

blocks.md:
- The main uses of radio and microwaves are for wireless communication

  - Many things people often assume use radio waves actually use microwaves (e.g., Wi-Fi, radar, mobile phones, satellite communications)
- At very high intensities, microwaves can also be used to heat food

  - This is what happens in a microwave oven

- Warm objects emit infrared radiation
- Infrared can be detected using thermal imaging cameras:

  - in security cameras, for research, and also in medicine
- Remote controls have small infrared LEDs that send invisible signals to an infrared receiver on a device such as a TV
- Infrared travels down fibre optic cables more efficiently than visible light

  - So most fibre optic communication systems use infrared

- Visible light is the only part of the electromagnetic spectrum that the human eye can see
- Visible light is used for photography, videography, and illumination

- Ultraviolet is responsible for giving the skin a suntan, which is the body’s way of protecting itself against ultraviolet rays
- When certain substances are exposed to ultraviolet light, they absorb and re-emit it as visible light (making them glow)

  - This process is known as fluorescence
  - Fluorescence can be used to secretly mark things using special ink
  - Most bank notes have invisible fluorescent markings on them
- Fluorescent light bulbs also use this principle to emit visible light

- The most obvious use of X-rays is in medicine
- X-rays pass through body tissues but are absorbed by denser body parts, such as bones

  - Bones absorb X-rays, leaving a shadow that can be seen using photographic film

- Gamma rays are used to kill cells and living tissue
- This property is utilised in both cancer detection and treatment

  - If gamma rays are carefully aimed at cancerous tissue, they can be effective at destroying the cancerous cells
- Gamma rays can also be used to sterilise food and medical equipment by killing off the bacteria

blocks.text: Summary of the uses and dangers of the electromagnetic spectrum

blocks.alt:
A blue continuous wave at the top shows decreasing wavelength and increasing frequency from left to right. Each type of wave points to a box containing its specific use. Radio waves are used for long-range communications because they can be reflected from the Earth's atmosphere. Microwaves are used for satellite communications because they can penetrate the Earth's atmosphere. Infrared is used for optical fibre communication because they can undergo total internal reflection. Visible light is used for taking photos and videos because cameras are set up to detect visible light. Ultraviolet is used for detecting security ink because it fluoresces with ultraviolet lighting. X-rays are used to photograph bones because they can penetrate soft tissues but not bone. Gamma rays are used to sterilise medical tools because gamma radiation kills bacteria.
Two larger boxes at the bottom outline the main dangers of electromagnetic radiation. High-intensity microwaves can cause heating of internal organs because water molecules absorb microwaves strongly. Gamma rays, X-rays, and high-intensity UV light can harm cells and cause cancer because they are highly ionising due to having a lot of energy.
